"Our protest had a diverse programme with both Palestinian and Jewish people on the stage, drawing attention to the ceasefire declared on 10 October 2025, which is not a ceasefire, since the genocide in Gaza continues every day." Red Line On 8 November a Red Line demonstration against the situation in Gaza is planned in Amsterdam. JA21 wanted the assurance that no one from <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> will be present there, because according to MP Nanninga the organisation of the demonstration is linked to Hamas. In the past, <entity id="person:rob-jetten">premier Jetten</entity> walked along at a Red Line event. Van Weel will discuss the issue in <entity id="org:ministerraad">de ministerraad</entity>, but he gave no assurance. The <entity id="org:directoraat-generaal-algemene-inlichtingen-en-veiligheidsdienst">AIVD</entity> states that Hamas has been involved in pro-Palestinian protests in the Netherlands, but according to Van Weel it is not established that this also applies to the Red Line demonstrations. "Of course it is not prohibited in itself to express your support for the Palestinian population. You do have to make that distinction", he said in addition.

title: No place for demonstrators on stadium grounds at AZ match against Israeli club
lead: For fear of confrontations between demonstrators, supporter groups and the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity>, the <entity id="org:gemeente-alkmaar">gemeente Alkmaar</entity> has designated a demonstration site outside the stadium grounds ahead of the football match between AZ and the Israeli club Hapoel Be'er Sheva. That Europa League match is being played Thursday evening. Two demonstrations have been registered with the municipality in connection with the match. The demonstrators may not stand at the stadium itself, but may stand across a busy road and roundabout. According to regional broadcaster NH, the new location is along a cycle path that many supporters use to cycle and walk to the stadium before the match. Two pro-Palestinian demonstrations: Mayor Schouten of Alkmaar shared in a letter to the municipal council this morning how the municipality is preparing for the Europa League match on Thursday at the AFAS Stadium in Alkmaar. The letter shows that two pro-Palestinian demonstrations are currently registered with the municipality. The demonstrators had indicated they wanted to stand in front of the doors of the AZ stadium, but neither the municipality nor the police are willing to allow that. Various factors: In the council letter, Schouten writes that she has received signals that Israeli supporters may still come to Alkmaar despite a municipal decision not to admit Israeli supporters. She also takes into account an announcement on social media by various AZ supporter groups in her decision, as well as the chance of a counter-demonstration and the "sentiments in society". The mayor fears confrontations between demonstrators, supporter groups and the police, vandalism, and insufficient safety for visitors if the demonstrations were to take place on the stadium grounds. "On the stadium grounds it is not possible to take sufficient control measures to prevent disorder, and it is not possible to separate visitors to the football stadium from the demonstrators," Schouten writes. The number of demonstrators expected is not known. "At the location where demonstrating is allowed, a safe arrival and departure of demonstrators can be better facilitated," Schouten writes. "It also prevents confrontations with other groups from taking place there." Risk profile: Late last month, Alkmaar decided not to admit Israeli supporters to the match. Although football association UEFA has assigned the Israeli club's supporters a 'medium risk profile', the municipality of Alkmaar classifies the match as a match with a "(very) high risk" "because of the geopolitical context". The municipality explicitly refers to the violent riots around the Ajax-Maccabi Tel Aviv match in 2024. The <entity id="pos:burgemeester-alkmaar">burgemeester van Alkmaar</entity> has been advised by the Amsterdam <entity id="person:femke-halsema">burgemeester Halsema</entity>. The decision caused outrage in Israel. The Israeli ambassador expressed "serious doubts about the justification" for the decision in a phone call with Schouten. The Israeli foreign minister also raised the matter with his Dutch counterpart Berendsen. Schouten announced yesterday that her decision stands.

title: OM demands six years in prison for man (23) who deployed fake agents 38 times
lead: A man from Nieuwegein is standing trial for committing fraud with fake agents. According to the Public Prosecution Service (OM), the suspect attempted 38 times to gain entry to people's homes via fake agents. It concerns one of the largest fraud cases involving fake agents, the OM says. The 23-year-old man is suspected of being active within a criminal organisation in which he directed people. The group is said to have operated nationwide. According to the OM, the suspect called victims and then passed their addresses on in chat groups. He allegedly used the names "Altijdstroom555" and "kkoeksss" on Snapchat. The man gave instructions to the fake agents within the group. They were then told by the suspect what was present in the house and what they should take. The suspect also gave tips to the fake agents, the OM says. For example, the man allegedly instructed them to "supposedly check locks and fittings in homes". In 26 cases the group succeeded in taking jewellery, cash and bank cards. In the other 12 cases it remained an attempt, the OM says. 'Living like God in France' The man was arrested last summer. He allegedly committed the fraud between September 2024 and July 2025. "In 29 cases the suspect played an active role, in 9 cases the role was passive in nature", says the public prosecutor. The suspect denies a large part of the accusations, but according to the OM there is sufficient and convincing evidence of his criminal activities. "He received a welfare benefit, was under administration, received 40 euros weekly pocket money, but could live like God in France without having to sweat for a boss", according to the public prosecutor. In addition to a prison sentence, the OM also demands that he pay 100,000 euros in damages to victims. Several suspects from the group have already been convicted. The court in Leeuwarden will pronounce its verdict on 30 November.

title: Polish shops remove Halloween accessories from shelves after stabbings
lead: In Poland several retail chains are stopping the sale of certain Halloween accessories following stabbing incidents at schools. Shopkeepers describe the sale as "inappropriate" given the stabbings. Biedronka, with some 3,900 branches one of Poland's largest retail chains, among others, has announced it will remove fake knives and creepy costumes. Children's retail chain Smyk has also said it will no longer sell plastic knives and cleavers, among other items. "Out of concern for the wellbeing of children and young people, we decided yesterday to remove certain Halloween products that may evoke undesirable associations from our range," Biedronka said. In a statement, Smyk indirectly refers to the recent stabbing incidents. "We believe that the presence of such items on the shelves of a store aimed at families is inappropriate under the current circumstances." Third stabbing incident: Last Saturday was the third stabbing incident in just one week at an educational institution in Poland. A 21-year-old woman injured three people: two 17-year-olds and someone aged 24. Earlier, a 19-year-old and a 15-year-old were arrested for two different stabbings in which several people were injured, and at a primary school one person also died. Online rumours also circulated that a "Bloody Friday" would soon take place. The Polish Minister of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-biza">Binnenlandse Zaken</entity> said that on Monday about 20,000 police officers had been sent to schools. According to Prime Minister Tusk, the massive deployment has helped bring the situation under control. According to the authorities, the attacks are not linked to an organised group. Instead, the government states that the glorification of violence online is harmful to young people. The Polish government is therefore trying to fast-track legislation that would make it easier to remove harmful online content.

title: Counter-terrorism prosecutor takes over investigation into French school shooter (14)
lead: The French counter-terrorism prosecutor has taken over the investigation into the 14-year-old pupil who shot at a teacher and the head of a secondary school in Aubagne, near Marseille, yesterday. That is what the French news channel BFMTV reports. According to the counter-terrorism prosecutor, there are indications that the boy drew inspiration from the True Crime Community, with which he appears to have ties. This online group glorifies extreme violence, sometimes resulting in violence. A childhood friend who spoke to the French newspaper Le Parisien says the suspect was obsessed with the shooting game Call of Duty and was in social isolation. The boy's father and mother have also been taken in for questioning. The father had numerous weapons lying around the family home, some of which were illegal. According to Le Parisien, the mother was questioned about the boy's plans. Guitar case: According to the authorities, he took a shotgun to school yesterday, hidden in a guitar case. The school staff he shot at were injured but are not in danger of their lives. Sources within the French Public Prosecution Service have told BFMTV that the boy expressed regret. He reportedly said it was revenge on the school staff, although he could not explain how he came to his actions. The headmaster's manner reportedly did not appeal to him.

title: Farmers' organisations want to talk to minister about their own nitrogen proposals
lead: The nitrogen letter from <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> should be scrapped and no longer require a permit everywhere. That is what the farmers' organisations united in the Landbouw Alliantie want, and they want to talk with <entity id="person:jaimi-van-essen">minister Van Essen</entity>. This afternoon they presented their plans at the Nieuwspoort press centre in The Hague. The chance that the minister adopts the plans seems minimal. First of all, according to the Landbouw Alliantie, the nitrogen letter from Minister Van Essen of last June must be scrapped. With that slogan, the farmers' organisations toured the country this summer to mobilise farmers for action and to inform them about what is hanging over them. With today's proposals, the alliance hopes to give farmers prospects and to bring the minister around. Compared with Minister Van Essen's nitrogen plans, according to the Alliance, very little is needed to solve the nitrogen problem. Whereas Minister Van Essen sent a thirty-page nitrogen letter to <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Kamer</entity> at the start of summer, the alliance mainly focuses on the stalled permit granting. The alliance consists of the farmers' activist group Agractie and the interest groups of dairy and poultry farmers (DDB, NMV and NVP). Paper problem Authorities can currently issue permits for activities that release nitrogen only to a very limited extent. The Landbouw Alliantie's solution is to change the rules so that many businesses no longer need a permit at all. They offer two variants: only businesses within 250 metres of overburdened nature areas need a nitrogen permit, or that obligation applies only to very large emitters. This is not possible under current legislation, emphasises Jan Venneman on behalf of the Landbouw Alliantie. The rules must first be amended. "It is a paper problem, so there must also be a paper solution possible," says Sieta van Keimpema of the DDB about this. Moreover, the Landbouw Alliantie does not want to get straight to work on nature restoration, unlike the minister. The farmers think that the state of nature areas and what is needed for restoration should be reassessed. After that, new management plans must be drawn up. Deterioration of nature "With this proposal you will not unlock permit granting," expects nitrogen expert Jan Willem Erisman of Leiden University, who followed the meeting digitally. He expects the alliance's plans to lead to more nitrogen emissions. "That leads to deterioration of nature, while we have a duty precisely to counter that deterioration." The most important points from the cabinet's nitrogen plans The plans that Van Essen presented at the start of summer include, among other things, stricter standards for livestock farmers and zones around nature areas where only very little nitrogen emission will be allowed in future. In the eyes of the Landbouw Alliantie, those plans will have disastrous consequences for agriculture. The minister holds weekly talks with the farmers' organisations LTO and NAJK. The organisations that make up the Landbouw Alliantie are not at that table. Anger about this also came up during the meetings last summer. Half an hour The minister sent the organisations of the Landbouw Alliantie an invitation two weeks ago, says Jeroen van Maanen, spokesperson for the alliance. "We did not respond to that. We thought: we will first present our plan, and if the minister then has questions, we can explain." Moreover, according to Van Maanen, Van Essen had reserved "only half an hour" for the farmers in his agenda. Far too short, the spokesperson says. "What does a half-hour conversation involve? With ten people you can just about finish a cup of coffee and then you have to leave again." Erik Luiten of Agractie says that a meeting between the minister and the Landbouw Alliantie is now scheduled for next week Thursday. "We then have a quarter of an hour more or so," says Luiten. Harder actions Talks with the minister do not mean that actions are off the table, however. "Willingness to take action among farmers is increasing, including for harder actions," says Van Maanen. Minister Van Essen has responded in writing to the Landbouw Alliantie's proposals. They are not entirely new to him and were also raised earlier in talks with Agractie, he writes. That farmers' organisation and the minister view "fundamentally differently" what is needed to make permit granting possible again, the minister said. Van Essen does not think the Landbouw Alliantie's proposals are a solution, but he is willing to talk with the farmers. "The package of measures as we presented before the summer is and remains the basis for that; we will continue working on that."

title: Lower House: no money for Veilig Thuis, first get things in order
lead: The House of Representatives considers it too early to give the reporting point Veilig Thuis the 70 million euros that its board requested today in an alarming appeal. This is according to a round of inquiries by NOS. First it must finally be examined what exactly is going on there, various factions say. The reporting point says it can no longer handle the large volume of work. VVD, D66, Pro and Groep Markuszower want to know where the problems at Veilig Thuis originated and what <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> will do to get things in order. The national Veilig Thuis network is the first and, for many people, often the only reporting point for domestic violence, child abuse, and the prevention of genital mutilation and femicide. The reporting point gives advice and investigates reports. But the waiting lists have been growing for years, and how Veilig Thuis works differs by region. How and how quickly your report is responded to depends on where you live. Reflection The House therefore adopted a motion a year ago, with support from all factions, calling on the cabinet to reflect on "the role, positioning and capacity" of Veilig Thuis. Especially since the cabinet itself emphasises the organisation's public importance. "Time to implement this House motion by the cabinet," says VVD MP Becker now. "More money is not the solution if we do not also fundamentally examine how this has been organised," D66 MP Synhaeve also believes." Pro MP Westerveld holds the previous and current cabinets to account for this. "This is not primarily a matter of money, but of doing what was promised." Situation has worsened In the year since the motion was adopted, the situation has worsened, the emergency appeal from Veilig Thuis shows. After a report, people must wait an average of two months. In some cases it is longer than six months, while by law action must be taken within five days. The board of Veilig Thuis itself speaks of passing reports around, partly due to waiting lists and shortages in youth care. The organisation wants more money to hire extra staff. "If it turns out that extra structural capacity is necessary to guarantee safety, then we must look at that seriously," says Kamerlid Moinat of Groep Markuszower. "But money must fund a solution, not just temporarily cover up the problem."

title: French schoolchildren's protest grows into a broader popular movement: 'This gives hope'
lead: "I am here to demonstrate and to stand up for my rights and those of my friends", says Adam Boucherca, second-year law student at the Paris-Panthéon-Assas university. For almost a month, demonstrators have been taking to the streets across France. Massive protests are also underway again today. At 5:30 a.m., Boucherca had arranged with friends to meet near the Paris university to set up a blockade. There they were met by a group of far-right youths armed with glass bottles, he says, while showing footage of it on his phone. "As we walked forward, they started throwing the bottles. I was hit on my elbow, and a friend of mine was injured." Discontent over rising costs. With a march to the official residence of Prime Minister Lecornu, demonstrators continue their action today. Along the way, students and teachers from other faculties join them. According to Boucherca, the protest has long been about more than problems in education. This is also evident from the presence of politicians from the radical left La France Insoumise (LFI) at the university blockade. "All polls show that Rassemblement National (RN) has a chance of winning the presidential elections next year", says Boucherca. That makes him afraid, he says. "This protest gives hope. It shows that French people are mobilising against it." What began as a schoolchildren's protest, and then gained support from students, has now grown into a broader popular movement. Many French people are dissatisfied with high fuel prices, rising housing costs and the policy of <entity id="org:regering">de regering</entity> in general. Demands submitted. The Franco-Dutch Suzanne Nijdam is chair of one of the largest French student unions. Together with other trade unions, she has submitted ten demands to the Ministry of Education, including extra investment. But the ministry has so far not responded to them. "It cannot be that so many students have to take to the streets again. Things must change, and it is up to the ministry to ensure that." Swedish climate activist Greta Thunberg also joined a protest at a secondary school in Saint-Denis, a suburb of Paris, today. A recent Ipsos survey shows how divided France is over the protests of recent weeks: 54 percent of respondents support the demonstrations, 40 percent are against. The older the respondents, the smaller the support. Politics in France is also divided over the protest movement. For example, supporters of La France Insoumise (LFI) and the alliance Socialist Party-Place Publique are most enthusiastic; supporters of Rassemblement National (RN), on the other hand, think there should be an end to the movement and the violence that comes with it. Got out of hand. That is also visible on the streets. At Paris-Panthéon-Assas university, among others, LFI parliamentarian Rodrigo Arenas is present. "All LFI parliamentarians are on the side of the students", he says. "We are here simply to ensure everything goes well and to monitor the conduct of the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity>." According to Arenas, the way the police have intervened at the protests has recently got out of hand. In his view, they have regularly overstepped the limits of what is allowed. More than 7,000 people have now been arrested, most of them minors. At Place Vauban, three kilometres further on, there were violent clashes with riot police: LFI parliamentarian Manon Aubry is also at the demonstration at the university to support the students. "That pupils taking part in demonstrations have been maimed for life should not happen in a democratic country where young people only stand up for their rights." Ange Lacour, himself a student, supports the demands of the demonstrators, but not the way they take action. "I have difficulty with the blockades that are set up without it always being clear what the demonstrators actually want to achieve." According to him, this is because the protest movement has no clear leader. Yellow vests. Meanwhile, more than half of French people think the protests will continue for a while. That is a setback for the government, which is trying to calm tempers by making promises, for example by calling up 3,000 substitute teachers. Trade unions have announced large-scale protests for Saturday, focusing on the widespread discontent in France. On social media, calls from the gilets jaunes to join the demonstrations are circulating. The well-known yellow vest movement paralysed large parts of France for months in 2018.

title: British security service sees Russia, Iran and AI as biggest threats
lead: In his annual speech, the head of the British security service MI5 named Russia, Iran and artificial intelligence (AI) as the main threats to the national security of the United Kingdom. He also said that threats from foreign adversaries have quadrupled over the past ten years. Roughly equal numbers of these involve hostile acts by states and by terrorist organisations. Russia MI5 chief Ken McCallum sees Russia as 'aggressor number 1'. According to him, that country is waging a war with non-military means to prevent NATO from responding militarily. According to him, the United Kingdom has expelled nearly a thousand Russian spies since the large-scale Russian invasion of Ukraine in 2022. Therefore Russian services such as the military intelligence service GRU now try to recruit Britons. 'So we see them paying criminals to carry out their assignments or exploiting naive people.' As an example, McCallum mentions the charge against a man who allegedly wanted to carry out an attack on a drone factory in the town of Swindon. 'It is no coincidence that Russia is trying to sow confusion in European countries at a time when its military gains in Ukraine are minimal and terribly costly.' Iran: Iran would operate in the same way. Over the past year, according to McCallum, fifty people have been arrested for activities linked to Iran. In many cases the Jewish community in the UK is said to have been the target. McCallum said nothing about the suspected preparation of an attack last month on the RAF base Fairford, while Prime Minister Burnham said yesterday that Iran was 'almost certainly' behind it. McCallum did address the threat from China. That country is reportedly guilty, among other things, of intimidating Chinese citizens living in the United Kingdom. That country would also use front companies to gather knowledge about AI. Weapons with AI: MI5 sees that threats to UK national security are increasingly using AI, including in the deployment of drones. What further concerns McCallum is that extremist groups are using AI to make biological weapons or to develop new types of biological weapons. As far as he knows, this has not yet succeeded. Terrorism: The terror threat in the UK was raised last spring to the level 'severe'. McCallum notes that the Islamic terror groups al-Qaeda and Islamic State are still capable of carrying out or having carried out terror attacks. The raising of the threat level earlier this year is, however, 'largely' due to the threat posed by far-right groups, says the security service. Those groups mainly target young people. MI5 recently investigated a radicalised 13-year-old. 'That investigation yielded information that allowed one of our international partners to prevent a deadly attack on its territory.'

title: Hijack report from aircraft cockpit to Germany turns out to be false alarm
lead: In the German city of Nuremberg, an aircraft landed safely after a hijack report was sent from the cockpit. The German air force then sent two fighter jets into the air. The hijack report turned out to be a false alarm. "From the cockpit, the code '7500' (hijacking) was transmitted, after which the pilot could no longer be reached by radio," the German police write. "For safety reasons, various alarms were subsequently activated." The Corendon Airlines aircraft had departed from the Greek island of Corfu and eventually landed in Nuremberg, the planned destination of the aircraft. The aircraft was escorted by two Eurofighter fighter jets. Air traffic at the airport was temporarily halted. Malfunction According to Corendon Airlines, a malfunction in the radio communication system caused the incorrect report. The airline stated that "there was no emergency situation and that the passengers, the crew or the aircraft were at no point in danger".

title: Empty shelves in no time: Albert Heijn outage shows how vulnerable the food chain is
lead: Not so much the production but mainly the distribution of products is a vulnerable point in the food security of the Netherlands. That is what experts say about the cyber incident at Albert Heijn , which halted operations and left supermarkets with empty shelves yesterday. According to Pieter Zwaan of research institute Clingendael, supermarkets and suppliers work so efficiently that there are almost no stocks to fall back on in case of incidents or disruptions. Zwaan investigated the vulnerabilities of the current food system on commission from the Ministry of Agriculture together with others. "In a situation like this, other supermarkets can offer relief for those who specifically want fresh products such as cauliflower or broccoli", says Zwaan. But in his view it is not unthinkable that if the outage at Albert Heijn had lasted longer, shortages would eventually have arisen at other supermarket chains such as Jumbo or Lidl as well. Eight days of home supplies Supermarkets and distribution centres together have a stock for about six days, says Zwaan, with a continuous supply of new products. He sees that supermarkets rely heavily on IT systems for the distribution of products, in order to get new stock exactly on time. These IT systems themselves are vulnerable to disruptions, as the cyber incident at Albert Heijn shows, but also because of their dependence on the power supply. In the report that the researchers of Clingendael and Erasmus University published last month, they concluded that the Dutch should therefore build an emergency food supply for eight days, not for three. One of the scenarios that was examined showed that in the case of a serious weather event, such as prolonged heavy rain, combined with a major power and IT outage, it could take as long as two weeks before the distribution chain is fully back up and running. Storage in city centres The researchers also write in the report that supermarkets must maintain an emergency stock with a minimum quantity of products for households so that they can keep a supply for eight days. Right now supermarkets do not have such a buffer at all, he says. Bart de Steenhuijsen Piters of Wageningen University & Research agrees. "Supermarkets have no stocks, and all their deliveries have to come from a central distribution centre", says the researcher, who specialises in food systems. "And that has a direct effect on what is on the supermarket shelves." Because food security is in the public interest, the government must think about how this vulnerability can be limited and what role stocks play in that, says Zwaan. "But the question is how that should happen. It is a political question of who will bear the responsibility." "It is also the question where those stocks should be kept, especially in places like city centres where space is limited", says Zwaan. Besides that, it is a cost issue, he says. "Because who has to pay for it: the supermarket or the government that wants them to hold extra stock?" De Steenhuijsen Piters explains that supermarkets are focused on efficiency, with the aim of keeping prices low for consumers and profit margins as high as possible for the company. According to him this has come at the expense of resilience, continuity and supply security. Yet stocks may also be sensible in these uncertain times from the perspective of supermarkets' profit margins, says Zwaan. "If you see how much turnover Albert Heijn is now missing, then it may be smart from a business economics perspective to keep a somewhat larger stock." Redistributing food In the event of a future major national shock, certain groups will be hit disproportionately hard, says De Steenhuijsen Piters. "According to the FAO (UN agriculture organisation, ed.) there are now 1.6 million people in the Netherlands who are food-poor and therefore have difficulty with their food supply and certainly with access to healthy food." To support this group, the government would then have to adopt a protocol to redistribute food. But such a national protocol does not yet exist. "And while shocks to the food system such as climate change, international conflicts and hybrid attacks are only increasing." Work on this is under way. This summer <entity id="person:silvio-erkens">staatssecretaris Erkens</entity>, who has Food Security in his portfolio, informed the House of Representatives in a letter that the government is working on plans to increase food security. "We know that our food system is uncertain, but we are not sufficiently prepared for it", says De Steenhuijsen Piters. He acknowledges that measures may come at the expense of profit margins, so investment in resilience will have to take place across the board. In his view, the realisation that they must work together on this is slowly sinking in. "We are at the start of that process."

title: Lung cancer found in Pope Leo, malignant nodule removed
lead: Pope Leo XIV has successfully undergone surgery for a small lung nodule, which turned out to be malignant. During the operation, lung adenocarcinoma, a common form of lung cancer, was identified. The lower part of his right lung has been removed, the Vatican reports . The operation lasted 90 minutes and, according to the Vatican, was successful and without complications. "The Holy Father has since returned to his room", the press office writes. The pope then woke up normally. The 71-year-old Pope Leo arrived earlier today at the hospital in Rome for the lung surgery . On Sunday he announced that a small nodule in his lung had been discovered during a medical check-up. Such a nodule, also called a nodule, is benign in most cases. In about 5 percent of cases it is malignant, according to the American Thoracic Society, an international organisation in the field of pulmonary medicine. Week in hospital It is expected that Leo will have to remain in hospital for a week. He has been admitted to the Gemelli Hospital, where popes are treated more often. All his audiences up to and including 20 October have been cancelled. The European Institute of Oncology advises against flying for three weeks after such a procedure. Whether the pope can make his planned trip to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru from 6 to 17 November depends on his recovery.

title: Groningen comes to the aid of Ter Apel and offers a hundred temporary reception places
lead: The municipality of Groningen will temporarily take in extra asylum seekers from tomorrow. It makes a hundred beds available at an existing emergency reception location on the Europaweg for families with young children. This is intended to relieve the pressure on the registration centre in Ter Apel. The extra reception has been arranged by the municipality of Groningen at the request of the ministry of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-am">Asiel en Migratie</entity>. Earlier today Minister Van den Brink wrote a letter to the House of Representatives in which he spoke of an "unsustainable" situation in Ter Apel. He asked all Dutch municipalities to "urgently create extra reception places". The situation in Ter Apel is again pressing. Last week twenty asylum seekers had to sleep outside in the grass in the rain, because there were too few reception places. Dispersal Act According to Groningen alderman Jalt de Haan, the situation is still acute and the pressure on the registration centre in Ter Apel is "unchanged and great". "The municipality of Groningen stands for humane reception of refugees and we do not want people to have to sleep outside out of necessity." Groningen already complies with the Dispersal Act, which regulates that municipalities take in asylum seekers in proportion to their size, and believes that other municipalities must also take their responsibility. "It is up to the national government to come up with a structural solution," says De Haan. Minister Van den Brink is pleased with the extra Groningen places and hopes that other municipalities will follow the example of the municipality. "They already do a lot there," he says in a response to news agency ANP. He also expresses his appreciation that Groningen is making room for families. "That is a vulnerable group." Three weeks The reception is initially intended for three weeks. What happens after that is not yet clear. According to De Haan's spokesperson, the situation will be reviewed if there are still insufficient reception places in Ter Apel in three weeks, or if no alternatives are available in other municipalities. Residents and businesses in the immediate vicinity have been informed by the municipality about the arrival of the families. Until recently, 150 asylum seekers were housed on the Europaweg. Most of them have since moved to another reception location. Currently forty unaccompanied minor asylum seekers are still staying at the Europaweg.

title: Penalty payments for asylum seekers disappear: large majority in Senate approves
lead: The Senate has in large majority agreed to two asylum measures that were earlier defeated. As a result, the <entity id="org:immigratie-en-naturalisatiedienst">Immigratie- en Naturalisatiedienst</entity> (IND) will no longer have to pay penalty payments to asylum seekers who have to wait too long for a decision on their stay in the Netherlands. Furthermore, it becomes easier to declare criminal asylum seekers 'undesirable' and deport them. That can now be done if they commit offences that carry a prison sentence of at least two years. Laws of Faber Both measures were part of the asylum emergency measures act of former asylum minister Faber (PVV). That law was voted down in the senate in April, because it also stated that illegal residence in the Netherlands would become punishable. Helping, for example, rejected asylum seekers would also be punishable. Asylum minister Van den Brink has nevertheless now achieved two other measures, the penalty payments and the expansion of the declaration of undesirability, via a detour. He linked them to another law, which was voted on today: the Return and Immigration Detention Act. That must regulate that more force can be used when deporting rejected asylum seekers. But also that their stay in detention centres becomes more humane. Nearly 100 million euro in penalty payments That last point is the reason that, for example, Pro, the largest party in the Senate, also voted for the law. Senator Thijssen finds the current detention regime for rejected asylum seekers far too harsh. That has even repeatedly led to suicide, she recalled, such as with Russian activist Dolmatov in 2013. Still, Pro is not in favour of abolishing the penalty payments, because they also act as an incentive for the IND to decide faster. A majority of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Kamer</entity> does want to get rid of them, because the amounts the IND pays out are rising sharply. Last year it concerned 79 million euro, while in the first half of this year the IND already paid out nearly 100 million euro. After the defeat of the asylum emergency measures act, Van den Brink promised to still get its content through parliament. That partly succeeded already with the introduction of the European Migration Pact, a few months later. Last week he came with the plan to make refusing to return to the country of origin punishable.

title: 'Iran steps up attacks on ships in Strait of Hormuz again'
lead: Iran has stepped up attacks on ships in and around the Strait of Hormuz this month. It concerns the largest series of attacks since the start of the American-Israeli attacks on Iran at the end of February, according to the British newspaper Financial Times (FT). Iran attacked six ships last Sunday alone, the newspaper writes based on the British maritime organisation UKMTO and European security sources. That would make it the day with the most Iranian attacks on ships in the strait since the start of the war. Five of the affected ships were oil tankers and the sixth was a container ship, reports the British maritime security company Vanguard. Two crew members of one of the oil tankers have gone missing, the Financial Times writes. Until now, early March was the most intense period in the Strait of Hormuz. In the first two weeks of that month there were thirteen attacks by Iran. In the first eleven days of October Iran hit a total of 24 ships, FT writes. High freight rates Shipping companies that were willing to sail through the Strait of Hormuz despite the high risk of attacks, because of high freight rates on other, longer routes, are avoiding the area again. Last Sunday only '2.9 million' barrels of oil were transported through the strait. In September oil exports were much higher at 15.5 million barrels per day, FT writes based on data from shipping data company Kpler. American attack Last Sunday the United States also attacked a ship in the Strait of Hormuz. According to the US, the ship departed from Iran and did not comply with the American blockade imposed on Iranian ports. The American statement cannot be verified. News agency Reuters tried to contact the owner of the ship, but was unsuccessful.

title: Explosives found in home of man who allegedly planned an attack on the Polish prime minister
lead: The man suspected of preparing an attack on Polish prime minister Tusk and defence minister Kosiniak-Kamysz had homemade explosives in his home. The Polish Public Prosecution Service announced this. The 66-year-old Krzysztof N. was arrested on Sunday after Polish security services raised the alarm. The Polish authorities called the threat "extremely serious". The Public Prosecution Service is charging him with nine offences. The main charge is conspiring to kill government officials with the use of explosives, prosecutor Skiba tells news agency Reuters. The suspect risks a prison sentence of two to ten years. No confession The man is also said to have been looking for people who would help him. He has not confessed and refuses to give an explanation for the explosives. He will be brought before a court tomorrow. Yesterday, a second suspect, a 46-year-old man, was arrested in connection with the same case. He reportedly called online for the murder of prominent politicians, including speaker Czarzasty of the Polish lower house.

title: 40 years in prison for former gang member behind the murder of Tupac Shakur
lead: The 63-year-old Duane Davis must serve at least 40 years in prison for the murder of American hip-hop legend Tupac Shakur. A judge in Las Vegas has ruled to that effect. Duane 'Keffe D' Davis was already found guilty of premeditated murder with a deadly weapon in August by a jury. According to the jury, it was proven that Davis had planned the murder of the rapper in 1996. He had supplied the firearm with which Shakur was shot. Tupac Shakur, better known as 2Pac, was shot in Las Vegas at the age of 25 while sitting in a car with his record boss Suge Knight. The rapper died six days later. At that time Shakur was world famous for hits such as California Love , Dear Mama and Keep Ya Head Up . After his death the song 'Changes' came out, which also became a worldwide hit: For decades it was a mystery who was behind the murder, and all kinds of theories circulated. Until Davis, a former gang member, spoke in interviews and in his 2019 memoir about his role in the shooting. Three years ago he was arrested . Memoir In his book, Davis had recorded, among other things, that Shakur and his entourage had beaten his nephew Orlando Anderson. He wanted revenge and drove around in a Cadillac with two others and his nephew looking for the artist. In 2008 Davis told the police, who investigated the case at the time, that he gave the firearm to someone in the back seat and that his nephew Anderson would have pulled the trigger. Prosecution ultimately did not follow because Davis had reached an agreement with the police. Anderson and the two other occupants have since died. In the courtroom, Judge Carli Kierny addressed Davis. "You can't just take a man away from his family. The world has never forgotten him." Davis has indicated he will appeal his conviction.

title: US ambassador leaves Greece after corruption allegations
lead: The American ambassador to Greece, Kimberly Guilfoyle, resigned today. President Trump said earlier this week that he had asked for her resignation after corruption allegations. Guilfoyle, formerly a presenter at Fox News, came under fire after reports that she asked a Trump donor to transfer 100,000 dollars so she could pay off her personal credit card debts. That reportedly happened a few days before the Congressional hearing on her nomination as ambassador. According to The Wall Street Journal, the donor did not comply with Guilfoyle's request. The paper also writes that after her appointment as ambassador, Guilfoyle boasted at the World Economic Forum in Davos about trips that "wealthy Greek businesspeople" would have paid for her. According to the paper she flew to Davos on a private jet and stayed at a luxury resort in Gstaad, Switzerland. Guilfoyle denies Guilfoyle denies the reports. She writes that the allegations are not true and that she is determined to "vigorously defend" her name, reputation and integrity. She also writes on X that her "dedication to President Trump, the 'America First' movement and the country I love will never end". "We asked Ambassador Guilfoyle to resign," said Katie Zacharia, the new White House spokesperson, today. "She has been of great value to the team and we wish her the best." Guilfoyle is the former fiancée of Donald Trump Junior, the president's son. She was appointed ambassador to Greece last year. Guilfoyle worked for Fox News as a presenter for a long time.

title: Spanish royal couple visits Ceuta 2.5 months after influx, 'was badly needed'
lead: King Felipe of Spain and his wife Letizia have visited the Spanish exclave of Ceuta. They did so 2.5 months after Ceuta was overrun by tens of thousands of people who had illegally crossed the border from Morocco. This caused great anger among residents of Ceuta, who felt abandoned by the rest of Spain. It was the first time since his accession in 2014 that Felipe visited Ceuta. On arrival, the royal couple took plenty of time to shake hands and seek contact with residents. In a speech, the king gave the people of Ceuta encouragement. Ceuta undeniably belongs to Spain and that is not up for negotiation, he said. "We will not leave you alone." At the same time, he spoke out in favour of good ties with neighbouring Morocco. Morocco, for its part, thinks that Spain should cede the exclaves of Ceuta and Melilla. The visit drew thousands of onlookers. Spanish flags were waved everywhere. In the municipality's official guestbook, the royal couple called the visit "something that has long been looked forward to" and said it was "badly needed". At the end of July, more than 70,000 mostly young migrants entered Ceuta from Morocco, by land and via the sea. It took some time before police and the army had the situation under control. The vast majority of the migrants quickly returned to Morocco. A few thousand remained behind in Ceuta. Among them were many minors. This month a migrant camp on the beach was also cleared. In the aftermath of the crisis, hundreds of thousands of people took to the streets in Ceuta and on the Spanish mainland, and pressure on Prime Minister Sánchez increased. Many Spaniards accused his government of doing too little about the situation in Ceuta. Meanwhile, attention to it has faded, partly because of the housing shortage protests. Islamic cemetery In Ceuta, the royal couple had a conversation with residents and officials about the events at the end of July. They also visited a school. Later they went to an Islamic cemetery, where they commemorated the 141 people who died trying to reach Ceuta. Aid organisations assume there are even more victims. The following day, the Spanish royal couple travels to Melilla, the other Spanish exclave on the North African coast.

title: Mars rover Perseverance sets distance record (but it is not fast)
lead: The Mars rover Perseverance of space agency NASA has set a record five years after arriving on Mars. Never before has a human-made vehicle driven so far on a planet other than Earth: 45,22 kilometers. Perseverance (perseverance) has thereby broken the old record of the Mars rover Opportunity. That little rover covered 45,16 kilometers between 2014 and 2018. Perseverance's average speed of 9 kilometers per year may not seem very impressive, but at NASA they are very proud of the achievement. The vehicle was supposed to cover about 20 kilometers on the red planet. The odometer now reads well over double that. And that is not the end of it: the Mars rover must keep driving until at least 2028. Curiosity is also still driving. Perseverance was sent to Mars five years ago to research the surface of the planet. The six-wheeled vehicle can map its surroundings itself and determine a safe route. All of that happens extremely carefully, and therefore slowly. What also does not help is that commands from the control center can take well over twenty minutes to reach Perseverance. NASA has one more vehicle on Mars, Curiosity. After sixteen years it has 38,15 kilometers on the odometer and will continue for a while longer. Curiosity is probably soon going to overtake the number 3 spot on the list of space rovers with the most kilometers. That spot is currently still held by the Russian moon rover Lunochod 2, which covered 39 kilometers and needed only a few months to do so in 1973.

title: Prison and TBS for series of offences ending in rape of 87-year-old woman
lead: A man from Ede must go to prison for eight years for a series of offences, including attempted manslaughter and the rape of an 87-year-old woman. The court also imposed a TBS order on the man, who is 27. The <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> had demanded thirteen years and TBS. The offences took place between August and October last year. The man first sexually assaulted a woman (34) in a forest near Bennekom. Two days later he sexually abused a 16-year-old girl. She was assaulted on a park bench. The man also committed several thefts afterwards. In early October the man broke into the home of the 87-year-old woman. She caught him inside the house at night. The man then lost control: he pulled her down the stairs and repeatedly threw her "like a doll" onto the floor, the verdict states. While she lay on the floor, he raped her several times. He then searched the house for items to take. He left the woman for dead. The woman was found the next morning by the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity>. They had been alerted by a concerned neighbour and family. The victim still suffers every day from the rape and the violence. Mental disorders The man has largely confessed to the offences. Research by the Pieter Baan Centrum shows that he has several mental disorders. According to experts, the man was severely diminished in criminal responsibility at the time of the offences. They therefore advised imposing TBS with compulsory treatment. The judge followed this advice. The TBS can be extended repeatedly, for as long as the risk of reoffending has not been sufficiently reduced. The TBS treatment begins once the man has served his prison sentence. He must also pay damages: 45,000 euros to the older woman and 2,000 euros to the 34-year-old woman he sexually assaulted.

title: Recording device found in OpenAI meeting room, employee arrested
lead: AI developer OpenAI has discovered recording equipment in one of its own offices. The American company speaks of a "sophisticated recording device". It had been placed in a meeting room in San Francisco where business-sensitive information is often discussed. OpenAI made the discovery at the end of September. The device was wrapped in toilet paper and was inside the USB port of a television. According to the FBI, which is leading the investigation into the case, it had probably been there for two days by then. The trail soon led to a Saudi employee of OpenAI. He was seen on camera footage near the meeting room, where he officially had no access. The man (35) is also said to have given instructions to an AI chatbot in the days before that related to making and storing audio recordings. Camera footage further shows the man searching behind the television in question. The recording device had already been discovered and removed by then. Years in prison threatened The Saudi man was arrested on 9 October. He faces up to five years in prison and a fine of up to 250,000 dollars. OpenAI has dismissed him immediately. The company says on X that it has no indication that he obtained valuable information. FBI director Kash Patel sees in the case proof that protecting American AI is essential for the nation's national security and economic prosperity. "The FBI therefore regards this mission as one of the highest priorities in the field of counterintelligence", he says in a statement from the American Department of Justice.

title: Strike in regional transport, impact differs by region
lead: Regional transport is on strike today. Travellers should expect delays and cancelled services. The impact differs by region. Due to the strike, no Arriva trains are running in Limburg. In other parts of the country, Arriva trains are running according to the timetable. For example, all trains between Zwolle and Emmen, between Almelo and Hardenberg, and between Zutphen and Oldenzaal are running. There are also no cancellations on the regional lines in Groningen and Friesland. In bus transport, the effects of the strike are greatest in North Brabant, where about 10 percent of buses are running, according to Omroep Brabant. At the central bus station in Tilburg, some people who were unaware of the strike stood there this morning. In Twente and Limburg, about 70 percent of buses are running. In the Achterhoek, there are no cancellations at all. Collective agreement negotiations The strike was prompted by the failure of collective agreement negotiations. Drivers and conductors at operators such as Arriva, Keolis, Qbuzz, Transdev and EBS have been called on by the unions to lay down their work. Office staff are also joining the strike. Urban transport in Amsterdam (GVB) and The Hague (HTM) does not fall under regional transport. Buses, trams and metros are therefore running as normal there. In Rotterdam, no buses are running, but trams and metros are. In Utrecht, about a quarter of buses appear to be running. There are also fewer tram services. What is running and what is not? Operators find it difficult to indicate which buses and trains are running and which are not. For example, Keolis says on its own website: "We only know shortly in advance which buses/trains will be running". Transdev also simply says it does not yet know what will be achieved. Like other operators, Arriva advises travellers to check the journey planner shortly before departure. Trade unions CNV and FNV called for the nationwide strike last week. They believe that the operators' collective agreement proposals amount to a deterioration. The operators, for their part, say that their financial scope is limited and that public transport must remain affordable. The unions themselves demand, among other things, 9.5 percent additional salary over a period of two years and better working conditions for older staff. If the employers do not give in, the unions say strikes will take place on a different day each week from now on.

title: Wake-up call 14/10: Bus strikes across the country • Nord Stream bombing trial begins
lead: Good morning! Bus passengers, take note: due to strikes, fewer buses are running throughout the country today. And in Germany, the trial over the 2022 Nord Stream bombing begins today. First, the weather: it is dry, and especially this morning the sun is regularly visible. Now and then high cirrus clouds drift over. This afternoon cumulus clouds also appear. With a weak to moderate southwesterly wind, it will be 16 to 18 degrees. Are you heading out today? Here you can find the overview of traffic jams and roadworks, and here everything about the situation on the rail network. What can you expect today? What did you miss? The man found guilty of the 1996 murder of rapper Tupac Shakur in the US must go to prison for 40 years. A judge yesterday set the sentence for Duane Davis (63). In August a jury already found it proven that Davis had planned the murder of Shakur. For decades all kinds of theories circulated about the murder of Shakur. Until Davis, a former gang member, spoke about his role in the shooting in interviews and in his 2019 memoir. Three years ago he was arrested. Davis is appealing. Other news from the night: And then just this: It was no longer really exciting after the 8-0 win on Saturday, but the Dutch women's footballers have now definitively qualified for the final round of the World Cup play-offs, next year. In Tilburg Hungary was again beaten: 3-0. In the last qualifying round Oranje plays two matches against Slovenia. The international break runs from 26 November up to and including 5 December, so by Sinterklaas evening at the latest Oranje will know whether the tickets to the World Cup can be booked. Missed goals? Watch our summary: Have a nice day!

title: Trial over Nord Stream attack starts today: 6 questions about 'sabotage of the century'
lead: The criminal trial against Ukrainian national Serhii K. begins today in Hamburg. He is charged with blowing up the Nord Stream pipelines between Russia and Germany in 2022. K. is alleged to have coordinated the sabotage of the most controversial energy project in Europe, on behalf of Ukraine. Because of its scale and impact, it is sometimes called "the sabotage of the century". Not everything about the background has been clarified yet. Was this, for example, an act of terrorism? Or were the pipelines a legitimate military target? And what role did the Ukrainian government play? Six questions and answers about the Nord Stream trial. How did K. go about it? In late summer 2022, the group around Ukrainian soldier Serhii K. rented an inconspicuous German sailing boat, the Andromeda, for several weeks, without a GPS tracker on board. From the port of Rostock, the ship then disappeared over the horizon for almost three weeks. During those days, in mid-September, divers from the group are alleged to have placed powerful explosives at several locations. A complicated job, at depths of tens of meters. "Professionals", according to the prosecutors. Before the explosives detonated, the group returned the yacht and left Germany. Shortly after 02.00 on the night of Monday 26 September 2022, powerful explosions were measured in the Baltic Sea. Gas bubbles became visible near the Danish island of Bornholm. The operation had succeeded: the explosions rendered three of the four pipes unusable. Nord Stream The Nord Stream gas pipelines between Russia and Germany have been controversial since the start of the project in 2005. Poland and Ukraine lost revenue from gas transport. Germany benefited from cheap Russian gas, but became dependent on the whims of Moscow. This became clear after the Russian invasion of Ukraine. In response to EU sanctions, Russia stopped the gas supply via Nord Stream 1. Nord Stream 2 had not yet been put into use. The German government has since ruled out restoration and commissioning. What evidence is there? Images of the white van in which the saboteurs drove to and from the port eventually led investigators to K. At border checks, it turned out he had been checked using a forged but traceable passport. He did not, however, feel he was in danger. K. travelled to the Italian city of Rimini in 2025 and could thus be arrested. In the Italian cell, K. himself provided the most incriminating evidence. In a telephone conversation with his wife, he reportedly spoke, according to the prosecutors, about admitting the sabotage operation as an "official military operation". That was supposed to prevent his extradition to Germany. This conversation was intercepted and now serves as the basis of the charges. Beyond that, there are more indications than hard evidence. For example, K. had two different passports, a sign that there was something to hide. His internet behaviour is said to show that K. searched extensively for information about critical infrastructure, specifically in the area around the Nord Stream pipelines. His smartwatch was switched off around the time of the sabotage. What is K.'s defence? K.'s German lawyers reject all accusations. Regardless of whether K. was involved in the operation, his defence argues that the German court lacks jurisdiction. The sabotage is probably the work of a state, and therefore an individual cannot be held responsible, K.'s lawyer Ilona Menaker told NOS earlier. The lawyers want the court to also rule on whether the pipelines were allowed to be in operation at all or were a legitimate military target. K. is the only person on trial. One of the divers, Volodymyr Z., was previously arrested in Poland but not extradited. This summer he was arrested again, this time in Croatia, where he is said to have attended the filming of a Hollywood film about the Nord Stream sabotage. What role does the Ukrainian state play? The German prosecutors state that there are "sufficient suspicions" that the sabotage was carried out on the orders of the Ukrainian state. What evidence exists for this is not known. According to Der Spiegel, the operation was approved by then commander-in-chief Zaluzhnyi. The plans reportedly were drawn up by a group of former commandos of the Ukrainian army. President Zelensky reportedly was not informed, while the Dutch military intelligence service <entity id="org:militaire-inlichtingen-en-veiligheidsdienst">MIVD</entity> reportedly was. The Netherlands had therefore already warned Germany and the US about the plans earlier, according to research by Nieuwsuur. Why is this case being heard in Germany? While Sweden and Denmark quickly discontinued their investigations, the German public prosecutor's office pressed on. Germany is treating the case very seriously, as the largest act of sabotage against German infrastructure since the Second World War. The pipelines were partly owned by German companies, and the operation was carried out from the German coast. The case causes a certain unease in political Berlin. Germany is Ukraine's most important ally. If involvement from Kyiv is proven, that would at the very least be painful for relations between the two countries. Pro-Russian parties such as the AfD and BSW want to stop supporting Ukraine, partly because of this issue. What sentence hangs over K.? Serhii K. is suspected of war crimes, causing explosions and damaging critical infrastructure, carrying a maximum sentence of fifteen years in prison. Hearing days are scheduled through February.

title: Costa Rica opens strict mega-prison following El Salvador
lead: Costa Rican President Fernández opens a new mega-prison in her country today. The prison in Alajuela, half an hour's drive from the capital San José, has room for over 5000 detainees. The opening of the prison is a new step in the fight the government of the Central American country is waging against organised crime. In building the prison, close attention was paid to the CECOT in El Salvador, a mega-prison with room for 40,000 prisoners. President Bukele of El Salvador even laid the first stone of the Costa Rican prison and will also attend the opening, as will his Colombian colleague De la Espriella. For formerly progressive Costa Rica, the measures in force in the new mega-prison are unusually strict. Family visits are prohibited, calling with mobile phones is not possible and prisoners are monitored with the most modern surveillance techniques. Each cell has room for a maximum of sixty prisoners. Transit route That Costa Rica, which was formerly known as the safest country in Latin America, is taking these measures is not for nothing. The country now has the second-highest murder rate in the region: this year over 640 murders have already been committed, exceptionally many for a country of just over 5 million inhabitants. Over 70 percent of those murders are attributed to drug conflicts. Costa Rica has grown over the past ten years into a prominent transit route for cocaine from South America. The Mexican cartels Sinaloa and Jalisco have gained a foothold there, as has the Colombian Clan del Golfo. Security has become such a major priority that President Fernández recently openly fantasised about deploying American ground troops to help combat crime. A record 21,000 Costa Ricans are now behind bars, and the new mega-prison has yet to be opened. Fernández hopes that children from poor neighbourhoods with drug problems will soon visit the mega-prison, on the assumption that the place will have a deterrent effect. But there is also opposition: supervisors in Costa Rica say there is a risk of human rights violations because independent oversight of the prison is lacking. The very fact that the prison was built on the model of the Salvadoran CECOT raises concerns. The mega-prison there has become a symbol of President Bukele's ruthless policy, who in 2022 declared a state of emergency that has since been extended more than 45 times and still applies. Since 2022, over 90,000 people have been arrested in the country, and reports of human rights violations and torture by guards emerge from Salvadoran prisons. Salvadoran NGOs report that at least 500 people have died in these prisons. More mega-prisons in the region Nevertheless, mega-prisons are in vogue in the region. Security is the biggest concern of voters in virtually all Latin American countries; (hard-)right candidates in particular boast of a tough approach to crime, inspired by Bukele. And since the right is winning elections everywhere in Latin America, large prisons are sprouting up like mushrooms. Leaders in Colombia, Honduras and Peru have announced the construction of such facilities, and in Ecuador, Panama and Guatemala construction has already begun. According to the platform InSight Crime, since the opening of the CECOT in El Salvador in 2023, plans for sixteen mega-prisons have been presented in no fewer than ten countries in the region. None of the prisons to be built is as large as the Salvadoran prison, which is probably the largest in the world. Experts meanwhile question the strategy of mass incarceration of criminals: in Brazil, Ecuador and Venezuela, gangs arose precisely within the walls of overcrowded prisons, and leaders continued their criminal activities from within. Democracy under pressure That Bukele did achieve results with his policy in El Salvador is probably explained by the fact that his entire government policy is focused solely on security. According to human rights organisations, probably thousands of Salvadorans are wrongly held. In addition, they have no access to lawyers and are tried in mass trials. Bukele has also used the state of emergency in his country to go after political opposition, critical press and NGOs. If other countries in the region that are rebuilding their mega-prisons fully copy Bukele's policy, democracy in Latin America could come under considerable pressure in the coming years. title: No cabinet plan yet on compensation for healthcare costs, uncertainty for chronically ill people
lead: What will happen with compensation for people with high healthcare costs? Today there is a debate in <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> on the healthcare budget, but it is still unclear how the cabinet wants to help chronically ill and disabled people. Because the first healthcare cut is due to be voted on at the end of this year, concern in this group is growing. "I find the uncertainty very annoying", says Bo Rijvers, who uses a wheelchair. "I know that blows will fall, but not yet how I am supposed to absorb them." Mainly uncertainty about the tax deduction It is mainly unclear how the tax deduction for healthcare costs will proceed. Under this scheme, people can claim costs for things like orthotic insoles, car adaptations and prostheses as a deduction and pay less tax. "For me that is 2000 to 3000 euros per year", says Rijvers. In the coalition agreement the cabinet agreed to scrap this scheme from 2028, because it is too complex and the money does not always actually reach chronically ill and disabled people. To compensate the low-income group for the healthcare cuts, 350 million euros has been reserved. But a concrete plan for how that money will be distributed still does not exist, while the Tweede Kamer has to vote on the budgets in a few weeks. "We are still studying it", says <entity id="person:eelco-eerenberg">staatssecretaris Eerenberg</entity> (Fiscal Affairs). A large majority of the Tweede Kamer asked the cabinet last month to examine whether the deduction for healthcare costs could be retained, but only for people who are truly chronically ill or disabled. Parties are mainly worried about the accumulation of cuts coming for this group in the coming years. For example, the cabinet plans to introduce a personal contribution for district nursing, to raise the own risk and to abolish domestic help under the Social Support Act (Wmo). Some people will as a result lose hundreds of euros per month, Nibud calculated earlier . Other consequences are also still unclear. Stopping the deduction could, for example, mean that chronically ill and disabled people receive less allowance. "You of course have to look at how we pay for the rising healthcare costs", says ChristenUnie-<entity id="person:mirjam-hannah-bikker">fractieleider Bikker</entity>, who submitted a motion on it. "But it cannot be that a group of people who already have it harder disproportionately pays the bill." Pro thinks the uncertainty is lasting too long. "People know their healthcare bill is going up, but not yet whether they will be compensated for it", says Kamerlid Julian Bushoff. Various political parties have little confidence that 350 million is enough for the new scheme, but staatssecretaris Eerenberg thinks it is. He says there are still many people using the schemes, while financially that does not need to be the case. He wants the money to be used only for chronically ill people who really need it. The target group will thereby become smaller, "so we think we should be able to get by with that amount." 'Kept me awake' Rijvers finds it mainly annoying that there has been so much uncertainty since the presentation of the coalition agreement. "At first it really kept me awake", he says. "But now that they don't know it themselves either, I think: why all this panic? I can't follow it." Eerenberg has let it be known that he will come up with a plan for the healthcare cost deduction within a month. The question is whether the Tweede Kamer can agree to it then. Several parties hinted that they could otherwise remove that measure from the Tax Plan, so that there is no vote on it at all this year. In that case the current deduction would certainly remain in place up to and including 2028.

title: Boat capsizes in India: thirteen children dead
lead: Thirteen children have died in a boat accident in India. The boat capsized on the Ganges river. According to The Times Of India, the children were on their way to a party. The rescue operation is still in full swing. The newspaper writes that three or four people are still missing. Seven other people on board have meanwhile been rescued and taken to hospital. It is not clear how the boat went wrong. Before the emergency services arrived on the spot, residents who saw the accident happen came to help. Prime Minister Modi of India has expressed his condolences to the relatives of the children who died. He also says they can expect financial compensation.

title: Good third quarter for ASML, further growth expected
lead: Dutch chip machine maker ASML has a successful third quarter behind it. Moreover, the company says it is already seeing interest from customers in ordering chip machines for the coming few years. "Many conversations with customers are now about the period after 2027," says CEO Christophe Fouquet at the presentation of the quarterly figures. ASML is benefiting enormously from investments in artificial intelligence and other technology that requires chips. ASML customers expect that they themselves cannot meet demand for chips until at least 2028, says Fouquet. "For us, that means more demand in the short term." According to its own account, ASML has already received many orders for 2028. "But there is also great interest in placing orders now for 2029 and sometimes even 2030." This means ASML has to work hard to meet demand for its chip machines. Three months ago the company said it must increase its capacity for EUV machines. ASML is the only company in the world that can make chip machines with this technology, which works with extreme ultraviolet light. The company earlier expressed the ambition to have 30 percent more capacity for these machines in 2027 than this year. In 2028 another 30 percent should be added on top of that. "But to be honest, it is becoming increasingly clear that 30 percent in 2027 and 30 percent in 2028 will not ensure that we can meet the demand from our customers," says Fouquet now. Sharp rise in profit. The sales of EUV machines are the biggest driver of the higher revenue and profit that ASML is booking. Over the past three months the company sold for 11.6 billion euros, partly through sales of new machines and upgrades of existing machines. Profit in the last quarter came to almost 5 billion euros. That is considerably more than in the same period in recent years: then the profit in the third quarter was consistently around 2 billion euros. "All in all, I would say it was a very, very strong quarter," Fouquet said. So far in 2026 ASML has made over 10.6 billion euros in profit. The company expects to ship 65 machines to customers this year, 50 percent more than last year. The company is also working on upgrades to its machines, so that customers can make more chips in the same period. ASML's customers include chipmakers TSMC, Samsung and Intel. ASML is one of the largest companies in the world and is of considerable importance to the Dutch economy. The Dutch chip industry has grown enormously in recent years, partly thanks to ASML, and provides tens of thousands of jobs. American bill. Alongside the challenge of meeting demand from the chip industry, ASML still faces an American bill that could practically halt the company's business in China. Supporters of the bill want to prevent ASML from supplying or maintaining its chip machines for China. ASML's financial chief Roger Dassen hopes that the American Congress will realise after the midterm elections in November that the proposal is not a good idea, reports ANP. In June, <entity id="person:sjoerd-sjoerdsma">minister Sjoerdsma</entity> of Foreign Trade already travelled to the US to discuss his concerns. He says the law will precisely ensure that China copies Western technology faster. China is expected this year to account for around 20 percent of ASML's business, the company says today.

title: Body 'forgotten' Frenchman has been lying in morgue in Toulouse for 14 years
lead: At the university hospital of Toulouse, a body has been found that had been lying in the morgue for about fourteen years. The regional newspaper La Dépêche discovered this. The man died in 2012 in his house in the village of Castelnau-d'Auzan. He was 58 years old. "We received a phone call on 1 October", says the mayor of Castelnau-d'Auzan to La Dépêche. "I thought it was a joke." After the autopsy in 2013, the <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> had already ordered that the body be released so that a funeral could be arranged. But the Frenchman's body never left the morgue. No family had reported itself. Therefore, it was the municipality's task to finish the matter. The municipality says it had received no response from the morgue at that point. Another scandal The body was found at the beginning of this month during an inspection of the cold rooms at the Hôpital Rangueil. That inspection of the morgue took place as part of an investigation by the Public Prosecution Service. According to the newspaper Sud Ouest, this was because of the discovery, at the end of last month, of the remains of two newborn babies and two foetuses. These lay in a container with medical waste from the morgue. Lonely The Frenchman is described as a lonely man. He was divorced, had no children and died a natural death. One of his neighbours raised the alarm at the time, when the man had not been seen for some time. A search has nevertheless been started to find relatives of the man.

title: Zelensky: over 600,000 Ukrainians without power after new Russian attacks
lead: Due to large-scale Russian attacks on Ukrainian energy infrastructure, more than 600,000 Ukrainians are without electricity. That is what President Zelensky says on X. Russia used ballistic missiles in the attacks on Kyiv and Kharkiv. According to Zelensky, Russia fired a total of 39 ballistic missiles and 120 drones overnight. An apartment complex was hit in Kyiv. Three people were killed and 22 were injured, The Kyiv Independent reports. After the attack a large fire broke out in a flat. Dozens of residents had to get out. Resident Maksym tells the Kyiv Independent that he and his partner fled to the corridor of their apartment complex to go to the shelter. They did so after the windows had blown out in an explosion nearby. "Everything happened very fast. We hardly realised what was happening", he says. Zelensky accuses Moscow of ignoring the ceasefire on energy facilities that US President Trump announced this weekend. According to President Zelensky, the Russians continue attacks on both power plants and critical infrastructure. "The attack was deliberate and demonstrative. Russia has never shown such contempt towards the US." Ceasefire: Other cities in Ukraine were also attacked overnight, such as Zaporizhzhia and Dnipro. Deaths occurred there and power plants were damaged. The attacks follow earlier Russian attacks on Ukrainian energy infrastructure, just as temperatures are falling and the heating season is approaching. Zelensky says, based on intelligence, that Russia is preparing more attacks with ballistic missiles. The Russian authorities say they hit a total of seven Ukrainian energy facilities and a data centre overnight. Destroyed power plants and apartment blocks sawn in half scattered through a city like Kyiv show how difficult it is for Ukraine to face this threat: Zelensky repeated today that Ukraine was not warned by its Western partners about the Russian launch of ballistic missiles. That usually does happen. The air raid alarm only sounded once the missiles were already on their way. Western intelligence services help Ukraine in the war against Russia by passing on intelligence about actions of the Russian army. Last year Trump ordered his services to stop doing that, after he had quarrelled with Zelensky. A week later the quarrel was settled and the intelligence flow resumed. 'No coincidence' That makes it all the more striking that an adviser to Zelensky said today that Ukrainian soldiers faced restrictions on Starlink, the satellite system of Elon Musk used among other things for drone operations, without warning. According to the adviser, the Ukrainian Ministry of Defence had not been informed in advance. "Our armed forces received no warning about these restrictions, which led to a number of missions failing. It is clear that this measure cannot be a coincidence and is related to the current political situation." With this he appears to refer to the recent diesel deal between the US and Russia, but also to the growing tensions between Ukraine and the US. President Trump is trying to pressure Ukraine into halting attacks on Russian oil and energy infrastructure, in the hope of driving down oil prices. title: Eighteen Ajax supporters arrested in Croatia, 'they had weapons on them'
lead: In the Croatian city of Split, eighteen Ajax supporters were arrested yesterday, Croatian media report. Photos and videos of the arrests are circulating on social media. The Amsterdam club plays an away match against Hajduk Split in the Conference League tomorrow. Footage from news site Tportal, among others, shows the supporters being arrested on a terrace in the centre of Split, after which they are taken away in police vans. Bladed weapons were reportedly found on the fans. Stone blocks can be seen on the terrace tables. According to Croatian media, it was a preventive action and the aim was to prevent the Ajax supporters from clashing with supporters of the home club, NH Nieuws reports. Physically attacked: The Ajax supporters' association reports that fans were attacked by supporters of Hajduk Split. Ajax also writes that it has received multiple reports this morning of "Ajax supporters who have been intimidated or physically attacked in Split". Taxi drivers reportedly passed on to Hajduk's hardcore group that they were transporting Ajax supporters, after which they are waiting for them when they get out. "In some cases their luggage has been searched for club symbols", the club writes. The <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> is said to be aware and to be present in greater numbers at the airport and in the city. "Please stay alert for your own safety", the club advises. Ajax had already warned its own fans in advance about safety risks. "Supporters of Hajduk Split are known for their fanatical following and may react to visible Ajax symbols or recognisable groups of Ajax supporters", the club said earlier. The match between Ajax and Hajduk Split will be played tomorrow at 18:45.
