title: Cabinet wants to take harder action against zoos that lag behind on animal welfare
lead: Zoos that do not keep up with new insights on animal welfare will soon be easier to take harder action against. In the most extreme case, withdrawing their licence could even be considered. That is stated in a new vision by State Secretary <entity id="person:silvio-erkens">Silvio Erkens</entity> of Agriculture. At the same time, he wants to make it easier for zoos that invest in, for example, better enclosures.

title: Russia declares Dutch platform RAAM an 'undesirable organisation'
lead: The Dutch knowledge platform RAAM, which shares information about Russia and Eastern Europe, has been formally designated by Russia as an 'undesirable organisation'. It is the first Dutch-language medium to be so designated. "At the very least, it means the Russians don't like what you are doing."

title: Public Prosecution Service leadership allowed prosecutors to ignore community service ban. But that plan was withdrawn at the last moment
lead: Anyone who commits the same criminal offence multiple times within five years may receive a community service sentence for it only once. But the College of Procurators General wanted prosecutors to ignore this statutory rule. After internal unrest, the plan was scrapped just before its introduction.

title: That is where the mice thrive in the cellar of Keetje Tippel
lead: Arjen Fortuin repeatedly takes a book from street book cabinets all over the Netherlands, discusses it, and passes it on. The old fortified town of Grave takes you straight to grimy Amsterdam.

title: Substitute Mexx Meerdink helps AZ to victory with a József Kiprich moment: 'Is that so? I don't know him'
lead: AZ has its first win in the Europa League. After a weak first half, it was ultimately a penalty that made the difference for the Alkmaarders. From eleven metres, substitute Mexx Meerdink became the hero and determined the final score of 2-1. He did something József Kiprich did in 1995.

title: Ebola threatens Kenya, but the country remains open to travellers
lead: Now that Kenya has confirmed a second Ebola infection, concern is growing about border controls and the risk of further spread. Many travellers are coming from Congo, where more than 4000 people have already died of the virus, via Uganda to Kenya.

lead: Track cyclist Harrie Lavreysen has become the first ever to win the keirin world title for the fifth time. The defending champion and Olympic champion thereby leaves British legend Chris Hoy definitively behind. The 29-year-old from Brabant took the lead at the right moment in the final in Shanghai and did not give it up again.

title: China policy requires one front
lead: The European Union has secured a first meaningful concession from China. Starting in December, only 350,000 hybrid and plug-in hybrid cars from the People's Republic may enter the EU in the first year. That is well over half fewer than are expected to arrive this year.

title: Establishment of municipal damage insurer temporarily paused
lead: The establishment of the Risicobeheerfonds has been temporarily paused. The fund was meant to provide collective damage insurance for municipalities, but it is not getting off the ground yet. Municipalities that have to renew their insurance therefore remain dependent on the private market.

The KNVB is not one of the council's 36 members and was not present.

title: Podcast De Dag: railway staff on suicide on the tracks

NS and ProRail are also very reticent in their communication about 'collisions on the tracks'. lead: Living permanently in holiday parks is a subject that has been causing debate for decades. The national government and the municipalities often do not see eye to eye on this. Elanor Boekholt-O'Sullivan, the current minister of Volkshuisvesting, calls on municipalities to be restrained in enforcing the rules, but the vast majority of municipalities are not listening, research by NOS shows. "As a municipality, at some point you no longer know what to do," says Albertjan Tollenaar, professor of Administrative Law at the Rijksuniversiteit <entity id="org:gemeente-groningen">Groningen</entity>, on Spraakmakers.

title: Housing budget is hard to spend
lead: That housing construction in the Netherlands does not happen by itself is shown, among other things, by the underspending of the budgets of the ministry of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-vro">Volkshuisvesting en Ruimtelijke Ordening</entity> (VRO). title: NASA's Mars rover sets off-Earth distance record
lead: NASA's Mars rover has broken the off-Earth distance record on Mars. Since 2021, the little vehicle has covered 45.2 kilometers on the planet. That is more than any other vehicle on a planet other than Earth.

lead: Polish authorities arrested a man on Sunday who is suspected of planning an attack on Prime Minister Donald Tusk. The threat is being taken "extremely seriously".

lead: "We must not let ourselves be distracted by people who want to make the rainbow flag political", said State Secretary <entity id="person:judith-tielen">Judith Tielen</entity> for Emancipation today. "It is not about politics, it is about everyone being able to be free and equal."

lead: Local administrators respond positively to the words that Prime Minister <entity id="person:rob-jetten">Rob Jetten</entity> spoke on Tuesday about cooperation and covering the costs of youth care by the national government.

title: Lawsuit in US over children's use of ChatGPT: 'They see it as a friend'
lead: Eight American states have jointly taken the matter to court because they believe ChatGPT poses a danger to children. They believe children are currently not adequately protected against the harmful effects of the chatbot. AI poses a risk to children, acknowledges Esther Rozendaal, professor of digital resilience at Erasmus University. "Children cannot yet think critically about the information they receive."

title: Former student Cornell gets police at her door after false tip about murders
lead: The woman who accuses students of Cornell University of gang rape received police at her door on Tuesday. Officers had been sent to her home after a false report of multiple murders at the address.

title: Call | Would you open your home to an asylum seeker? We are looking for you
lead: Last week twenty asylum seekers in Ter Apel had to sleep on the grass because the day shelter was full. Would you like to help solve the reception problems by taking in an asylum seeker at your home? Then we are looking for you.

lead: A good tax system is not designed in a month. The Netherlands must dare to invest in a reform that strengthens trust in society.

title: Schreuder hopes NEC fans stand behind Tadić and his team
lead: Dick Schreuder hopes the supporters of NEC will stand behind Dušan Tadić and his team. The coach of the club from Nijmegen said this a day before the Europa League match against Levski Sofia, in response to questions during the press conference about remarks by the Serbian footballer. In an interview with NU.nl, Tadić had said that the standard at Ajax was different from that at NEC.

title: Pope Leo XIV discharged from hospital after surgery for lung cancer
lead: Pope Leo XIV left the hospital on Saturday. On Tuesday, part of his right lung was removed from the 71-year-old church leader because he had a malignant nodule there.

title: Unrest in Pakistan after dissolution of the only provincial government with Imran Khan's party
lead: The Pakistani government has dissolved the administration of the northwestern province of Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa. According to the government, the provincial administration is colluding with the Pakistani Taliban. Critics call the decision a power grab to sideline the party of former prime minister Imran Khan.

title: France causes headaches in Brussels: no money, but it also says no to cuts
lead: The unpredictable situation in France makes the negotiations over a new EU budget extra complicated. Many European leaders want an agreement before Marine le Pen possibly takes over from Emmanuel Macron. But then the French will have to move a little too.

title: Municipalities and provinces can do more to protect migratory birds
lead: Municipalities and provinces can do more to prevent the extinction of vulnerable migratory birds. That is what Karsten Schipperheijn, managing director of Vogelbescherming Nederland, says.

title: 'Exceptional' ring with image of world wonder surfaces in Egypt
lead: Archaeologists have unearthed a ring with a special image near the Egyptian city of Alexandria. The jewel depicts the Lighthouse of Alexandria, one of the seven wonders of the world. The tower has very rarely been depicted. The lead researcher calls it an "exceptional" find.

lead: Tijjani Reijnders scored his first goal in the Asian Champions League on Monday. The midfielder was on target in the away match against Pakhtakor Tashkent in Uzbekistan. His goal proved not enough for victory: the match ended 1-1.

title: Overijssel: a deal is a deal regarding the Nedersaksenlijn
lead: The province of Overijssel has called on minister <entity id="person:vincent-karremans">Vincent Karremans</entity> to abide by the agreements made about the Nedersaksenlijn. 'A deal is a deal,' says deputy Martijn Dadema. 'We have raised all kinds of expectations among residents. It does something to the relationship between citizens and government when you don't keep such important agreements.'

title: Return hubs for rejected refugees: 'A total black box'
lead: Five European countries, including the Netherlands, are working on an initiative to send rejected asylum seekers to a country outside the European Union. Those reception locations are also called return hubs. The Greek asylum minister announced this week that the project will start in early 2027. The first refugees may go to Rwanda. But we then distance ourselves from all human rights. "As soon as you outsource that responsibility, it is completely, completely out of our hands", says Member of the European Parliament for Volt Anna Strolenberg in De Rode Draad. She has just returned from the area and tells what she saw there.

lead: A 71-year-old man was killed on Friday by an alligator more than 3.5 metres long in the American state of Florida. The man was fishing in an area known for its alligator population when the animal dragged him away.

title: 911 dispatch centre doubted authenticity of report on failed execution of Christa Pike
lead: Medical assistance to American Christa Pike, who survived an execution attempt at the end of last month, was delayed due to confusion at the 911 dispatch centre. Recordings show that emergency services doubted the authenticity of the report from the execution chamber.

title: Minister of Agriculture: understanding for worried farmer, but 'plans stay in place'
lead: The new nitrogen plans of <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> are causing great gloom among Dutch livestock farmers. As many as 87 percent say that because of the plans they have less confidence in the future of their own farm. Minister of Agriculture Van Essen responds today with understanding for the concerns, but stresses that the plans remain in place.

title: Latin festival Pal Mundo made a loss of 7 tonnes after 'fatal' setbacks
lead: The bankrupt event organiser Pal Mundo International made a loss of over seven tonnes last summer on the eponymous Latin American music festival in Almere. Despite the involvement of former Mysteryland manager Milan Raven, a lot went wrong.

AI objections add extra work for municipalities
lead: Municipalities, hospitals and public transport companies are increasingly dealing with objections drafted with the help of artificial intelligence (AI). The texts are generally longer, more legalistic and regularly contain incorrect references to legislation. This causes extra work and delays in handling objections.

title: Van der Eijk referee for Juventus in Europa League
lead: Referee Sander van der Eijk has been appointed by UEFA for the match between Celta de Vigo and Juventus in Thursday's Europa League fixture. The Dutchman will be assisted in Spain by assistant referees Rens Bluemink and Stefan de Groot. Allard Lindhout is fourth official. The VAR duo consists of the Englishman Michael Salisbury and the Dutchman Richard Martens.

Trump drops Russia sanctions and tariffs that Congress had approved
lead: US President Donald Trump is dropping heavy import tariffs on Russian energy. These had been approved by Congress in a law named after the late senator Lindsey Graham. According to Trump, they go against the national interest.

title: Choice for maintenance is right, but not at the expense of our water plan
lead: The state of many Dutch waterways and bridges is nothing to be proud of. It is right that <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> is freeing up money for the large backlog of maintenance. But that this comes at the expense of plans to protect us against drought is asking for new problems, writes political reporter Hans van Soest in this commentary.

title: NHG limit rises to 500,000 euros, buyers of homes with a low energy label 'have to get to work'
lead: Anyone who buys a home with a poor energy label and wants to benefit from the Nationale Hypotheek Garantie has to 'get to work' afterwards. NHG adds 20,000 euros to the loan as standard so that necessary sustainability measures can be carried out, the organisation announced today. The NHG limit itself also rises sharply, to 5 ton.

title: Another person dies after infection with West Nile virus in the Netherlands
lead: In the Netherlands, another person has died after being infected with the West Nile virus. This is the tenth person this year to die after infection with the virus, the <entity id="org:rijksinstituut-voor-volksgezondheid-en-milieu">Rijksinstituut voor Volksgezondheid en Milieu</entity> reported on Thursday.

lead: Against all odds, the global economy continues to grow. But the risks of AI, trade conflicts and government debt are piling up.

title: Dutch track sprinters retain World Championship title in Shanghai
lead: The Dutch track sprinters have once again successfully defended their world title in Shanghai. Harry Lavreysen, Jeffrey Hoogland and Roy van den Berg beat the Australians in the final of the team sprint. Since 2019, the Dutch trio has become world champion eight times in this event. For Lavreysen, it was his 21st world title on the track.

lead: For years, photographer Bieke Depoorter travelled around Egypt, Russia and the United States and slept at people's homes. What stands out in particular is the resemblance between the bedrooms; the more or less universal nature of the human sleeping place.

lead: Two ships have been attacked by drones off the coast of Bulgaria. One of the two ships has sunk, and eleven crew members from that boat are still missing. The fifteen crew members of the other boat have been rescued.

title: Bertram wants to combine public transport and other types of transport in the region
lead: Public transport and, among other things, pupil transport must be combined in regions where accessibility is declining. State Secretary <entity id="person:annet-bertram">Annet Bertram</entity> (Infrastructure, CDA) wants in this way to move from public transport to 'public mobility' that can be booked by everyone all day, she writes in a letter to the House of Representatives.

title: Two ships sank in the Strait of Hormuz, containers floating at sea
lead: Two ships have sunk in the Strait of Hormuz. They were struck by something, but it is unclear whether it came from Iran. According to Iran, one of the ships hit a mine.

title: AI agents of OpenAI boss Sam Altman hack their way through the internet by accident: is he keeping the technology in check?
